This article explains the identity and provenance choices that make a
`readagau` result reproducible. It uses the package's small, package-owned
synthetic workbook fixture, so it never contacts an official website. The
fixture has the shape of an Australian Crop Report workbook but its values are
not official source data.

## Discover once, then pin an exact release

Release discovery is metadata work. The bundled catalogue can be inspected
offline, while `refresh = TRUE` asks `readagau` to revisit the publisher's
landing pages. The result of a discovery is a release manifest with an exact
`release_id`, date, landing page, and asset roles:

```{r discover-releases}
library(readagau)
library(knitr)

cache_dir <- tempfile("readagau-source-cache-", tmpdir = tempdir())
dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE)

releases <- list_agau_releases(
  products = "crop_report",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
latest_row <- releases[which.max(releases$release_date), , drop = FALSE]
kable(data.frame(
  release_id = latest_row$release_id,
  release_date = latest_row$release_date,
  landing_url = latest_row$landing_url,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
))
```

`latest` is a convenient selector, not a durable identifier: a later
discovery can change which release is newest. For an analysis, record the
exact ID returned by discovery (and the source hash) in the analysis metadata.
`compare_agau_vintages()` also requires exact releases; it rejects `latest`
because a moving selector cannot define a stable comparison.

## Local files have a checksum identity by default

Passing a local workbook is the deterministic, offline path. If no release
metadata is supplied, the reader deliberately does not infer an official
release from a filename, file date, or workbook contents. Instead it uses a
checksum-qualified ID of the form `local-<first 16 SHA-256 characters>` and
leaves `release_date` missing:

```{r local-checksum-identity}
state_path <- system.file(
  "fixtures", "workbooks", "crop-state.xlsx", package = "readagau"
)
stopifnot(nzchar(state_path), file.exists(state_path))

reported <- read_crop_report(
  c(state = state_path),
  assets = "state",
  view = "reported",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)

local_identity <- data.frame(
  identity = unique(reported$release_id),
  release_date = as.character(unique(reported$release_date)),
  rows = nrow(reported),
  sha256_prefix = substr(unique(reported$sha256), 1L, 16L),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
kable(local_identity, row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(
  grepl("^local-[a-f0-9]{16}$", local_identity$identity),
  is.na(reported$release_date[[1]])
)
```

If the bytes have been matched to an audited edition, supply both values
explicitly. Supplying only one is rejected with an `agau_validation_error`,
because an ID without its date (or a date without its ID) is ambiguous:

```{r explicit-release-identity}
exact_id <- "acr-2026-06-02-no-218"
exact_date <- as.Date("2026-06-02")

official_identity <- read_crop_report(
  c(state = state_path),
  assets = "state",
  view = "reported",
  cache_dir = cache_dir,
  release_id = exact_id,
  release_date = exact_date
)

kable(data.frame(
  identity = unique(official_identity$release_id),
  release_date = unique(official_identity$release_date),
  rows = nrow(official_identity),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

The explicit identity is a provenance assertion by the caller. Make it only
after matching the bytes to a reviewed release; it does not turn a synthetic
fixture into official data.

## Reported and canonical views

The same bytes can be read in two intentionally different views. `reported`
retains the source presentation and its `record_role`; `canonical` applies the
package's versioned precedence rules where multiple physical rows represent
one semantic observation. Canonicalisation is within a product and does not
silently merge unrelated products:

```{r reported-canonical}
canonical <- read_crop_report(
  c(state = state_path),
  assets = "state",
  view = "canonical",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)

view_summary <- data.frame(
  view = c("reported", "canonical"),
  rows = c(nrow(reported), nrow(canonical)),
  record_roles = c(
    paste(names(table(reported$record_role)), table(reported$record_role),
      sep = ":", collapse = "; "),
    paste(names(table(canonical$record_role)), table(canonical$record_role),
      sep = ":", collapse = "; ")
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
kable(view_summary, row.names = FALSE)
```

Both views retain `source_dataset`, `source_sheet`, `sha256`, parser version,
and semantic fields. Use `reported` when auditing a source layout or preserving
every presentation; use `canonical` when joining observations across
workbooks under the documented precedence policy.

## Content-addressed raw and parsed cache

Raw assets are immutable. Their path is organised as
`raw/<product>/<release_id>/<sha256>/<asset>`, and the manifest records the
source URL, source filename, detected format, retrieval headers, size and
validation status. Parsed results use a separate key containing the release,
source hash, parser profile, dataset, selected sheets, and view. A changed
byte sequence therefore creates a new raw object instead of overwriting old
evidence.

The next example seeds an exact-release cache from the packaged local fixture
using the package's cache writer, then calls the public exact-release download
function. The second call is a cache replay: it has the same hash and does not
need discovery or network access. The internal writer is used only to make the
offline demonstration self-contained; normal online use populates the same
layout through `read_crop_report()` or `download_agau_release()`.

```{r cache-replay}
manifest <- readagau:::agau_cache_asset(
  product = "crop_report",
  release_id = exact_id,
  asset_type = "state",
  source_url = state_path,
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
replay <- download_agau_release(
  product = "crop_report",
  release = exact_id,
  assets = "state",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)

cache_summary <- data.frame(
  asset_type = manifest$asset_type,
  detected_format = manifest$detected_format,
  hash_directory = basename(dirname(manifest$local_path)),
  sha256_prefix = substr(manifest$sha256, 1L, 16L),
  replay_same_hash = identical(manifest$sha256, replay$sha256[[1]]),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
kable(cache_summary, row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(
  identical(manifest$sha256, basename(dirname(manifest$local_path))),
  identical(manifest$sha256, replay$sha256[[1]])
)
```

Use a project- or session-specific `cache_dir` in reproducible jobs. The
default `agau_cache_dir()` is a managed `tools::R_user_dir()` location; it is
not the working directory and is not a place to store credentials. `refresh =
TRUE` is an explicit request to look for new source bytes. It never mutates a
previous hash-addressed object.
